answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The pigment multiplier is published, charged in anchor, and quill lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3536 identities would post 3607 proofs and burn roughly 10 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
